## What the verify asserts instead of the fold checks

Replacing "the fold opens above / the count is the affordance":
- **every rendered tag is actually visible — none is hidden** (rendered count === `:visible` count)
- **no fold affordance exists anywhere** (`.pin-chip.is-more`, `.pin-fold`, `.is-folded` all count 0) — the anti-residue guard
- **with many tags the area WRAPS to more than one line** (distinct chip `top` values > 1) rather than hiding any
- **the composer still sits where it did** even though the tag area grew
- **the tag area never grows past its share of the pane**

Plus a new popover block (10 checks): opens a `role="dialog"` and **not** an in-place panel, floats above the shelf, names the run with the derived count, caps at 34vh, **costs the shelf no height** (row/tags/composer all unmoved), and closes by Esc, click-away and its own `×`. M2b now asserts explicitly that a long pin still opens **in place, not as a popover**.

Three assertions were re-based from top to **bottom** edges (tag line, composer): with `flex-wrap` a top edge legitimately moves when a line is added, so for bottom-docked chrome the bottom edge is the true "did it move" — a stronger claim, not a weaker one. The dismissal check likewise now asserts survivor **identity and order** rather than pixel position, since a wrapped area necessarily re-flows when six chips leave it.

## Two defects the run surfaced, both fixed

1. **Unbounded wrapping pushed the composer 7px below a 470px pane** (measured: bottom 888 → 907 against a 900px viewport). `.pin-tags` is now capped at 25% of the *measured* pane and scrolls inside itself. This is **not** the fold returning — every tag is rendered, nothing is `display:none`, there is no count chip, and at one-to-three rows it never engages. **Flagging for your call:** it is the one case where a tag can sit below a scroll line.
2. **The ResizeObserver effect had `[]` deps and ran once while the shelf was still rendering `null`** (M1.7), so it bailed permanently — `--pin-detail-max` *and* `--pin-tags-max` had been silently sitting on their CSS fallbacks since the original implementation. The fallbacks were close enough to the real values that nothing looked wrong; only the new 25%-of-pane assertion caught it.
